predecessors.name: Later Liang
predecessors.text: the Northern Liang breakaway: the Zhangye, Jiuquan and Dunhuang oases of Hexi

successors.name: Northern Liang of Gaochang
successors.text: the Juqu exile regime at Shanshan, then Gaochang, 442-460: The Juqu fled and occupied Gaochang

ledger.x: 397: Duan Ye is installed at Jiankang as Northern Liang prince.
398: the capital moves from Jiankang to Zhangye.
400: Li Gao breaks away at Dunhuang.
401: Jiuquan and Liangning go to the Western Liang.
412: Guzang becomes the capital: 'In 412, he made the city his new capital' and elevated himself to King of Hexi.
420: Jiuquan falls to the Northern Liang.
439: Northern Wei takes Guzang and the Northern Liang is ended.
440: the Juqu hold out in the west, with Jiuquan as capital.
441: the last Juqu seats in the western oases pass to Wei.

wars.name: Western Liang's rising against the Northern Liang
wars.outcome: Li Gao is acclaimed at Dunhuang and Jinchang in 400; Jiuquan and Liangning surrender to him in 401.

wars.name: Mengxun's war against the Later Liang
wars.outcome: Mengxun, allied with the Southern Liang, destroyed Later Liang in 403; the Sixteen Kingdoms page says the Later Liang gave its remaining territory to Later Qin in 403.

wars.name: Northern Liang-Southern Liang war
wars.outcome: Rutan invaded in 407 and was routed; failed Southern Liang campaigns 408-410; Mengxun besieged Guzang in 410 and its people surrendered in 411.

wars.name: Northern Liang-Western Qin clashes
wars.outcome: After the Western Qin took the Southern Liang in 414 the two met and 'fought with each other on multiple occasions' (Western Qin page); Liang pressure drove Mumo to Dinglian in 429.

wars.name: Northern Liang conquest of the Western Liang
wars.outcome: Jiuquan falls in 420 and Dunhuang in 421; the Western Liang ends.

wars.name: Northern Wei conquest of the Northern Liang
wars.outcome: Wei besieges Guzang and Mujian surrenders in 439; Wuhui's Juqu hold Jiuquan (440-441) and Dunhuang (441-442) before fleeing to Gaochang in 442.

certainty.note: The Hexi corridor is a chain of oases between desert and mountains; the page names Jiankang, Zhangye, Guzang, Jiuquan and Dunhuang only and no frontier with the Tuyuhun, the Rouran or the Western Qin.
